```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Table 2 of Balzer *et al.* (2021) reports the finite-sample performance of
the Two-Stage TMLE under the paper's main simulation: 500 replicates of
a 30-cluster CRT with post-baseline causes of missingness. This vignette
reproduces the Two-Stage TMLE rows of that table.

The vignette is set to `eval = FALSE` because each replicate is slow
(Stage 1 fits Super Learner inside every cluster, then Stage 2 fits a
TMLE with cross-validated APS). Allow ~30 minutes of CPU for the full
500 replicates. To run it quickly while developing, set `nReps <- 50`.

```{r setup-libs}
library(TwoStageTMLE)
library(data.table)

set.seed(1)
J <- 30
n <- c(100, 150, 200)
nReps <- 500
sl_library <- c("SL.mean", "SL.glm", "SL.gam")
```

## Compute the population truth

A large counterfactual sample (5000 clusters) gives us the true population
risk difference and risk ratio for comparison.

```{r truth}
pop_truth <- TwoStageTMLE:::get_truth_pop(
  do_complex = TRUE, effect = TRUE, n = n, J = 5000
)
pop_truth
```

The paper reports `RD = -9.1%` and `aRR = 0.88`.

## Run the simulation

For each replicate: simulate one trial, run Stage 1, run Stage 2 with APS
twice (RD with break-match, aRR keeping the matches), record point
estimate / SE / coverage / rejection.

```{r sim}
rows_rd <- vector("list", nReps)
rows_rr <- vector("list", nReps)

for (rep in seq_len(nReps)) {
  X_all <- TwoStageTMLE:::gen_data_complex(effect = TRUE, n = n, J = J)
  O <- TwoStageTMLE:::get_obs(X_all, exclude = FALSE)

  stage1 <- TwoStageTMLE:::stage1_tmle(    # internal reference impl (Balzer 2021)
    data = O,
    ind_cov = c("X1", "X2", "M"),
    clust_cov = c("X1.c", "X2.c"),
    sl_library = sl_library
  )
  s2_in <- copy(stage1); s2_in[, Y := tmle]
  s2_in <- add_weights(s2_in, target = "clust")

  # Match the paper's APS setup: no 'U' in the candidate list; always remove
  # the q-selected variable from g candidates (questions_for_laura.md Q14).
  clust_cov <- c("X1.c", "X2.c")
  cand <- list(
    cand_q_adj = as.list(clust_cov), cand_q_form = rep("glm", length(clust_cov)),
    cand_g_adj = as.list(clust_cov), cand_g_form = rep("glm", length(clust_cov))
  )

  rows_rd[[rep]] <- stage2_tmle(
    data = s2_in, goal = "RD",  target = "clust", break_match = TRUE,
    do_data_adapt = TRUE, remove_pscore = TRUE,
    cand_q_adj = cand$cand_q_adj, cand_q_form = cand$cand_q_form,
    cand_g_adj = cand$cand_g_adj, cand_g_form = cand$cand_g_form,
    psi = pop_truth$RD
  )
  rows_rr[[rep]] <- stage2_tmle(
    data = s2_in, goal = "aRR", target = "clust", break_match = FALSE,
    do_data_adapt = TRUE, remove_pscore = TRUE,
    cand_q_adj = cand$cand_q_adj, cand_q_form = cand$cand_q_form,
    cand_g_adj = cand$cand_g_adj, cand_g_form = cand$cand_g_form,
    psi = pop_truth$aRR
  )

  if (rep %% 25 == 0) message("rep ", rep)
}

results_rd <- rbindlist(rows_rd)
results_rr <- rbindlist(rows_rr)
```

## Summarise

For each scale, average the point estimate, its bias, the Monte-Carlo SE,
the average SE estimate, coverage, and power.

```{r summary}
summarise <- function(res, true_psi, on_log_scale = FALSE) {
  pt   <- mean(res$est)
  bias <- mean(res$est - true_psi)
  if (on_log_scale) {
    sigma_mc <- sd(log(res$est))
    sigma_ee <- mean(res$se)
  } else {
    sigma_mc <- sd(res$est)
    sigma_ee <- mean(res$se)
  }
  ci_cov <- mean(res$cover, na.rm = TRUE)
  power  <- mean(res$reject)
  data.frame(pt = pt, bias = bias, sigma_mc = sigma_mc, sigma_ee = sigma_ee,
             ci_cov = ci_cov, power = power)
}

cat("TMLE on the risk difference (break match):\n")
print(summarise(results_rd, pop_truth$RD), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nTMLE on the risk ratio (keep match):\n")
print(summarise(results_rr, pop_truth$aRR, on_log_scale = TRUE), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Expected results

From Table 2 of the paper (the two Two-Stage TMLE rows):

| Scale | pt | bias | σ (MC) | σ̂ (avg) | CI cov | power |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RD, break match  | -9.8% | -0.7% | 0.046 | 0.038 | 98.8% | 52.8% |
| aRR, keep match  | 0.9   | 0.0   | 0.051 | 0.058 | 96.8% | 57.8% |

The package's output will match these to within Monte Carlo noise
(500 reps is enough to get the second decimal right).
